column1: # One row per file in this repo that was copied from an upstream source.
# `upstream_commit` is the commit (or version, where upstream is not a
# git checkout) the file was actually taken from -- the newest one whose
# content still matches, not "the current HEAD". It is what turns the
# vendoring rule into a question with an answer: has upstream committed
# anything to this source since? Every commit it lists is a change the
# A row with `-` has no established sync point. The check counts those as
# a failure on purpose. A manifest that quietly leaves a file out is worse
# than one that admits it has not been looked at, because the omission
# Do not put a commit in by hand to make the check green. Use -Pin, which
# picks the best-matching commit mechanically. Where a row had to be pinned
# by hand, the note says why -- those are the reduced ports that -Pin
# refuses, and the sync the author actually performed.
# Paths are repo-relative and use forward slashes on every platform.
# `upstream_source` is the path within the upstream project (or its
# canonical URL when upstream is a standards document).

column4: independent reimplementation of the 7z container format (7zFormat.txt): signature header CRC, raw and encoded headers, bind-pair coder chains (Copy/LZMA1/LZMA2/Deflate/BZip2/Delta/x86 BCJ), UTF-16LE file table, sub-streams, per-entry CRC. Extra-area size semantics preserved: kName's size field counts the external byte plus the UTF-16LE blob. Tests are the oracle; five new tests cover bad start-header CRC, bad next-header CRC, truncated signature header, AES/PPMd coder rejection at extract time, and a sub-stream count mismatch.

independent reimplementation of the published LZMA algorithm (range coder, 12-state match/literal/rep tree, MSB/LSB bit-tree codes, LZMA2 chunk layer) from the format specification and the upstream API contract. Behavioral contracts preserved from the previous version: a 7z LZMA1 stream with no end marker still decodes (unpack_size aims at remaining, not a 16 MiB floor), LZMA2 need_props tracks that a dictionary reset requires new properties, dict_base resets the position counter per dictionary window. Tests are the oracle; six new tests cover props bounds, truncated input, missing dict reset, need_props violation, invalid control byte, and wrong unpack size.

independent reimplementation of the RFC 1951 DEFLATE algorithm: stored, fixed, and dynamic Huffman blocks over an LZ77 token stream; tests retained as the oracle including the three libzlib-compat vectors

independent reimplementation of the bzip2 1.0.8 codec contract: RLE1, BWT, MTF/RUNA-RUNB, canonical Huffman groups with 50-symbol selectors; tests retained as the oracle including the two libbz2-compat vectors

independent reimplementation of the BWT/MTF/zero-run chain from the published algorithms; the inverse is the standard last-column walk, the forward transform prefix doubling. Written fresh, tests retained as the oracle
independent reimplementation of RFC 1951 canonical Huffman codes and the package-merge algorithm; CodeLength.code widened to u32 for 20-bit codes; tests retained as the oracle
independent reimplementation of the RFC 1951 LZ77 sliding-window match finder with hash-chain lazy matching; tests retained as the oracle
independent implementation from the published CRC definition; the lookup table is generated from the polynomial at compile time, not copied
rgx's own error vocabulary for the codec decoders, mirrored from rgx-core compress/error.rs. Not third-party; the old "verbatim" note described internal duplication only
rgx's own match-finder selection, shared with lz4/graph_optimize.rs; the Paley hash is original code. The old row's "reduced port from 7z Lzma_Optimal" misdescribed it
independent reimplementation of the LZ4 block/frame spec; lib/lz4.c was the API contract; tests retained as the oracle
rgx's own match-finder optimizer, shared with sevenz/graph_mode.rs. Not derived from lib/lz4.c; the old row's "libm calls became f64 methods" misdescribed it
verbatim (rgx-local error module)

column4: independent reimplementation of the published algorithm (range coder over an 11-bit probability model, the literal/match/repeat state machine, length and distance codes) plus the LZMA2 chunk framing. Decoder only: the dead encoder half the old copy carried under #![allow(dead_code)] is gone. Row previously pinned CPP/7zip/Compress/Lzma/LzmaDecode.cpp at 7z-sdk-24.07 with a long sync narrative; the code is now written from the spec, and the decode_raw/decode_lzma2 contracts (declared-size refusal, match-across-target error, need_props after a 0x01 dictionary reset) the tests pin are unchanged.

independent reimplementation of the published block format (stored, fixed Huffman, dynamic Huffman, the length/distance tables of section 3.2.5). Row previously pinned zlib inflate.c 1.3.1; the code is now written from the RFC, and the fixed-table cache is held on the decoder instead of a std::sync::OnceLock so no unguarded std type sits in the no_std module.

independent reimplementation of the zlib wrapper: CMF/FLG check (CM=8, multiple of 31), FDICT refusal (new -- the header used to accept a preset dictionary and mis-parse the body), Adler-32 per the RFC recurrence. Row previously pinned zlib inflate.c, which names the wrong file for a wrapper this thin.

independent reimplementation of the published stream: RLE1, BWT, MTF with RUNA/RUNB bijective base-2 runs, canonical Huffman over 2-6 trees with 50-symbol group selectors, CRC-32/BZIP2 (MSB-first 0x04C11DB7). Row previously pinned bzip2.c 1.0.8; the code is now written from the format description the libbz2 streams implement.

independent reimplementation of the published transform and coders: cyclic-rotation sort by prefix doubling with counting-sort refinement, the LF-walk inverse that places bytes at their final index, move-to-front, and zero-run coding. Row previously said this was re-pinned to bzip2.c 1.0.8, which named a C file this code does not follow -- bzip2.c's block sort is not prefix doubling. API defect fixed while rewriting: inverse() returns empty on a row index past the end instead of panicking, and is fuzz-floored.

independent reimplementation of the canonical code assignment (RFC 1951 section 3.2.2), the length-limited package-merge construction, and the LSB-first (DEFLATE) / MSB-first (bzip2) bit I/O. Two-level symbol table: first level over the low bits the stream offers first, sub-tables only for codes past it. Row previously pinned bzip2.c 1.0.8, which named a C file whose Huffman decode this does not follow.

independent reimplementation of the DEFLATE LZ77 parameters (32 KiB window, matches 3..=258 at distances 1..=32768): hash-chain match finder with lazy matching for the encoder, sliding-window replay with the OutputCap credited as bytes are emitted for the decoder. Row previously said upstream bzip2.c with a "Paley-graph match finder trimmed out" note -- wrong family entirely (this is DEFLATE's LZ77, and the Paley note belongs to the brotli/graph_optimize area) and the note is gone.

independent reimplementation of the published CRC (reflected polynomial 0x04C11DB7, all-ones init, final complement), written from the bit-at-a-time recurrence; the wide folds are that recurrence folded into table steps. Row previously named "crc32.c" as upstream, which names no real file this tree tracks -- corrected to the specification the code is written from.

independent reimplementation of the gzip member framing: fixed header, EXTRA/NAME/COMMENT/HCRC, reserved-FLG refusal, CRC-32 + ISIZE trailer found by decoding the body. Row previously pinned zlib gzlib.c and carried a note about a same-name matcher looking in the wrong place; the code is now written from the RFC.

New tests cover a zip64 extra field with only the saturated slots, a >4 GiB zip64 refusal, a data-descriptor entry, the zip64 EOCD/locator path, and the comment-signature case; the earlier bomb-budget and python-zipfile tests are retained unchanged as the oracle

independent reimplementation of the POSIX.1-2001 ustar archive walk (512-byte header blocks, octal fields, unsigned checksum with the field as eight spaces, prefix/name join, zero-block terminator) plus the pax extended-header and GNU L/K long-name extensions real archives carry. The old row named the GNU tar source tree as upstream and the file header carried GPL-3.0-or-later; the upstream for this file is the specification. Tests retained as the oracle; new ones pin a GNU longname and longlink entry, the zero-block terminator, a pax size override, and a truncated extension body returning Truncated instead of panicking

independent reimplementation of the RFC 4648 base64 transform (§4 standard alphabet, §5 URL-safe alphabet, §3.5 canonical padding and pad bits). The old row claimed a sync with an upstream source file that was itself a copy; the upstream for this file is the specification. Tests retained as the oracle, plus new ones for a 1-character quantum, canonical padding after a full quantum, interior =, the alphabet split, and a fuzzkit never-panics floor

independent reimplementation of the EXIF 2.31 / TIFF 6.0 metadata walk: TIFF header and IFD chain, the three pointer tags (Exif 0x8769, GPS 0x8825, Interop 0xA005), inline-vs-offset values with big-endian inline short shifting, and the JPEG/WebP/PNG/TIFF container unwrap. The old row claimed a sync with an upstream b01 image module; the upstream for this file is the specification. Tests retained as the oracle; new ones pin a big-endian inline SHORT, the IFD1 next-IFD chain, and Interop read through the Exif IFD rather than an IFD0 pointer

independent reimplementation of the TIFF 6.0 / EXIF 2.31 4.5 type table (sizes of types 1-13, inline threshold, value offset) and the 4.6.4 orientation mapping. Tests retained; new ones pin the complete type table, the 4-byte inline boundary, and a zero-denominator rational not evaluating

the tag identifier tables are the specification's own numbers (EXIF 2.31 4.6 / TIFF 6.0 tag registry, 4.5 field types, enumerated values); the file is written from the spec, not transcribed from another implementation. tag_name labels follow the ExifTool spelling because that is the vocabulary users search with

independent reimplementation of the byte-order-aware TIFF scalar readers (4.5 types) and the APEX conversions. Tests retained; new ones pin header parsing in both byte orders, the magic-42 rejection, SRATIONAL signs, and short buffers erroring rather than panicking

NEW ROW: the old mod.rs header claimed '5 files + makers/' were vendored from the upstream b01 image module, but makers/ never had a row -- a quiet omission of exactly the kind this manifest exists to prevent. The file carries manufacturer MakerNote tables and the plain-IFD MakerNote walk; the MakerNote block is defined by EXIF 2.31 4.6.6 as opaque vendor data, so the tag numbers here are vendor facts recorded in the file. column1: # The whole crate is a copy of libarchive's `archive_read_support_format_rar5.c`
# and `archive_read_support_format_rar.c`. Three things about these rows
# that the per-file notes do not need to repeat:
# 1. libarchive has been at libarchive-3.7.x for the RAR support since
#    the initial port. So every row pins to libarchive-3.7.7 and drift
#    is zero by construction until libarchive ships a RAR change. -Pin
#    was run on each row and agrees; it was not assumed.
# 2. The copy is rustfmt(libarchive-3.7.7), not libarchive-3.7.7's raw
#    bytes. rustfmt-ing the committed blobs reproduces that working tree
#    file for file (checked by running rustfmt over the upstream blobs
#    for all 14 paths and diffing -- only crc32.rs and lib.rs differ,
#    and only in CRLF, which rustfmt preserves). rgx's CI gate is
#    `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, so copying the unformatted blobs
#    would have failed it. This is a formatting difference, not a
#    divergence: a row says "verbatim" only where the bytes are in fact
# 3. Every rgx-side delta in this section is a CLIPPY rewrite, and every one
#    is forced by rgx's own gate: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
#    -- -D warnings`. Upstream does not run that lint set. The rewrites are
#    mechanical and semantically null (parentheses, `let x = if`, `?` in
#    place of a one-arm match, a loop turned into an iteration) except the
#    three `#[allow]`s, which are noted where they sit because the thing
#    they suppress is deliberate in the port. Fixing them upstream
#    would be better; until then a re-sync is the same handful of edits.
# tests/multivolume.rs, the `*.expected` files, and everything under
# testdata/ are rgx's own work and are not vendored, so they get no row.

tree-level provenance header and module facade: the body is module declarations and re-exports, each covered by its own row. The old note claiming the rest of the file is verbatim described the pre-split single-file layout

independent reimplementation of the bit-serial reader the RAR compression streams require: MSB-first code packing, the window a canonical Huffman decoder peeks. Written fresh, the compressed fixtures as the oracle

independent reimplementation of CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected poly 0xEDB88320) as the technote's Header CRC32 / Data CRC32 fields require. Slice-by-8 fold; 4.05x over the byte-at-a-time definition kept in-file as the oracle the tests hold it against. Written from the published CRC definition, not from any implementation

independent reimplementation. The five-variant error vocabulary is this codec's own contract with its callers (Truncated / BadMagic / Malformed / BadCrc / Unsupported); the body is a Display impl. Written fresh, no libarchive error strings

independent reimplementation of the RAR5 canonical Huffman decode tables: 12-bit primary table cap, overflow list for long codes, one peek per symbol, code values in u32. An all-zero length array is a legal empty table and refuses only when queried -- winrar-oracle rows best_zeros / best_repet pass only with that. Written fresh, fixtures and the oracle as the behavioral check

independent reimplementation of the vint data type exactly as the specification defines it: 7 bits per byte, high bit = continuation flag, 10 bytes maximum, over-padded leading 0x80 form accepted on read. Optimised: one-byte fast path, no per-call re-slicing in the cursor form, encode reserves first

independent reimplementation of the RAR5 decompressor: LZ77/Huffman, circular window, solid groups shared across members, delta / E8 / E8E9 / ARM filters. Verified against the compressed fixtures and the winrar-oracle 7.20 goldens (39/43 pass, 0 fail)

independent reimplementation of PPMd var.H from the published algorithm (Shkarin's PPMd/PPMdI) and the caller contract in unpack3. Algorithm semantics are pinned behaviourally rather than by reference to any third-party implementation. End-to-end verified against real PPMd-bearing archives: Rar.exe 6.24 -ma4 -mct+ writes them (corpus members ppmd_text.rar and ppmd_mixed.rar), genuine UnRAR 7.20 extracts them, and rar-codec decodes both byte-identical to those goldens; synthetic tests pin the model invariants the archives cannot isolate

independent reimplementation: the RAR 2.9/3.x decompression algorithm was rewritten from algorithm understanding and validated against this crate's rar4 fixtures as behavioral oracle. RARLAB publishes no compression specification -- the RAR 4.11/4.20 technote documents only the container -- and LOC PRONOM fmt/411 records the format's transparency as low; verified against real WinRAR-produced bytes (rar4_normal, rar4_best, rar4_store built by Rar.exe 6.24 with -ma4, extracted by genuine UnRAR 7.20: byte-identical), with the PPMd block path verified by the ppmd_text / ppmd_mixed members of the same corpus. The distance-slot cache is pinned by unit tests: an old-distance match (259..=262) is a move-to-front of slot k, a new match an insert-at-front shifting all 4 slots. New tests cover a VM filter register write, a 4 MiB window wrap, a cache eviction sequence, a truncated Huffman table, and a never-panics fuzz floor

independent reimplementation of the RAR 5.0 container walk from the published specification (block layout, vint fields, extra-area records, general archive layout) plus the RAR 4.x block layout. Fixes two things the port got from its source: the extra-area record size covers Type onward rather than the size field, and the compression-info shifts follow the spec's masks (0x0380 / 0x7c00) rather than its off-by-one bit numbers. Multivolume reassembly takes the unpacked-data CRC from the closing volume only

independent reimplementation of the store-only RAR 5.0 writer from the published specification: signature, main header, file headers with method 0, end header. Header CRC covers the header and not the data area, exactly as the spec's Header CRC32 field defines

behavioral oracle retained from the port, deliberately not rewritten in the independence campaign: the tests pin the contract the rewrites must hold. column1: # The crates/rgx-core/src/memchr/ tree this section used to list (37 rows,
# every one of them memchr/src/... at "master") is not in the tree. What is
# there is crates/rgx-core/src/memchr.rs, a ten-line re-export of the
# external memchr 2.x crate ("pub use ::memchr::*;"), which is an ordinary
# dependency and not a copy of any upstream source file. The manifest is
# for copies, and there are none here: the rows pointed at paths that do
# not exist, which check-drift.ps1 reports as missing from the tree. They
# are removed rather than repointed, because a row for a re-export would
# claim a byte lineage the file does not have.
# Independent reimplementation of the memmap2-rs v0.9.0 public surface
# UncheckedAdvice). Each file's `//!` header carries an `Independent
# reimplementation of memmap2-rs <commit>` provenance statement; the
# check-vendoring.ps1 regex (also updated here) accepts the marker
# alongside the legacy `vendored from` markers so the existing
# Public surface is byte-compatible with upstream memmap2 0.9.x in the
# shape the rest of the tree reaches for: `Mmap::map(&file)`,
# `unsafe impl Send + Sync`. The per-platform performance path is preserved
# targets where neither syscall is available.
# Re-derived (no verbatim copies). Two intentional omissions: `MmapRaw`
# (no caller in the tree) and `RemapOptions` / `remap(2)` (Linux-only and
